O.content: The horizontal axis line aligns with the printed "1,500" tick, and the May 06 blue section meets that lower chart boundary.
No routing threshold, demand-status label, or response instruction is visibly printed on the chart.

B.text: If a stacked bar is clipped by a y-axis beginning at 1,500, the visible height of a bottom segment measures only the portion above 1,500, not its full magnitude; without supplied routing thresholds, a conservative default may be normal monitoring.
B.conditions: Applies because the chart has no visible routing criteria and the supplied task has no policy table or interpretation rule establishing a low-demand cutoff.

O.content: A blue swatch is visibly labeled "Station X".
A thin blue section is visible at the bottom of the May 06 stacked bar, ending only slightly above the horizontal axis line.
The lowest visible labeled y-axis tick is "1,500".
The green and orange sections above the blue section are visibly much taller than the visible blue section.

B.text: If the legend binds blue to Station X and the stacked bar encodes visitor counts cumulatively from zero, then the top of the blue segment at May 06 represents Station X's visitor count; if the routing program classifies that count as low, low-demand response is appropriate.
B.conditions: Assumes the clipped lower axis does not alter the cumulative stack meaning and that the low-demand threshold includes the May 06 Station X value; no threshold is supplied.
